correctness.rationale: The Eulerian even-degree interval-coloring parity obstruction forces the total edge count even, hence the number s of odd petals even. For each even petal two hub colors differing one admit alternating colors; for each odd petal differing two admit the explicit alternating adjacent ±1 sequence. Pair hub colors of each parity for odd petals and reserve adjacent pairs for even petals. If s odd, a single unused even hub color 2k becomes a pendant edge, producing an interval coloring using all 2k+1 colors. This proves def=s mod2; the standard weak local<=local<=def inequalities and absence of zero local gaps when noninterval give both other deficiencies. Valid for all finite k≥1, each cycle length≥3. Independently checked 780 constructed bouquets; finite tests do not establish full theorem.
